title: CFTC Sends Proposal To Regulate Crypto Transactions Following Clarity Act Fail
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

CFTC Sends Proposal To Regulate Crypto Transactions Following Clarity Act Fail
The regulator has already sent a proposal to the White House following this week's failed vote. 
This post CFTC Sends Proposal To Regulate Crypto Transactions Following Clarity Act Fail first appeared on...
content:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Thursday sent a proposal to the White House to regulate crypto transactions and markets. 

It isn’t clear what the regulations will look like from the post on the Office of Management and Budget’s website. The proposal is titled “Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets.”

The CFTC’s move comes after lawmakers blocked the long-awaited crypto legislation Clarity Act on Tuesday. Despite the law not advancing, both the CFTC and Securities and Exchange Commission have said they would go ahead with crypto rulemaking anyway. 

CFTC Chair Mike Selig said on Wednesday that while the Clarity Act didn’t move forward, the watchdog would still help U.S. President Trump “get the job done” in regulating the crypto space. 

“The outcome of yesterday’s Senate vote was unfortunate,” Selig wrote on X, adding that the CFTC was “locked in and ready to ship its rules for the new frontier of finance.”

Before the procedural vote on the legislation this week, Selig had said would proceed with rulemaking whether or not the Clarity Act is enacted — with the aim of finalizing rules before the administration’s term is out.

Senators last year approved Selig as the regulator’s chair. Formerly chief counsel at the SEC’s Crypto Task Force, Selig was described by White House’s Crypto and AI Tsar, David Sacks, as “instrumental in driving forward the President’s crypto agenda” 

President Trump campaigned on a ticket to help the crypto space after regulators under the previous administration hit digital asset businesses with lawsuits — mostly for allegedly selling unregistered securities. 

Since Trump became president, the SEC and CFTC have taken a much friendlier approach to watchdogging the space. 

The CFTC isn’t the only regulator going ahead with rulemaking: the SEC earlier this week approved tokenized stocks trading. In August, it also proposed its own framework for crypto asset offerings, pressing ahead while the landmark legislation stalled. 

President Trump last month urged lawmakers to pass the Clarity Act, calling the legislation “very powerful” — but Republicans said that Democrats were deliberately holding it back.  

Democrats mainly took issue with the ethics side of the bill. Trump received backing from major industry players while campaigning and since becoming president, his family has made money from digital asset ventures. 

Some lawmakers have alleged conflicts of interest. The White House has always denied any wrongdoing. 

A new draft of the bill started circulating in July tackling the issue of ethics and banning officials from making money from crypto. But some Democrats said it didn’t go far enough. 

The Clarity Act wants to formally divide oversight between regulators, distinguishing which digital assets are securities, commodities or stablecoins. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Why Is Crypto Up Today? Bitcoin Tops $80,000 as Ethereum, XRP and Dogecoin Rise Up to 7%
summary:
The crypto market is up today (Friday), with Bitcoin back above $80,000 and Ethereum, XRP and Dogecoin rising 6% to 7%. Bitcoin traded at $80,914 on Binance at 18:07 UTC, up 5.9% on the day, while Ether rose 6.4% to $2,603, XRP gained 7.3% to $1.39 and Dogecoin added 7% to $0.0874 on Bitstamp.
The m...
content:
The crypto market is up today (Friday), with Bitcoin back above $80,000 and Ethereum, XRP and Dogecoin rising 6% to 7%. Bitcoin traded at $80,914 on Binance at 18:07 UTC, up 5.9% on the day, while Ether rose 6.4% to $2,603, XRP gained 7.3% to $1.39 and Dogecoin added 7% to $0.0874 on Bitstamp.

The move comes two days after the Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time since 2023 and three days after the Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act. Neither shock broke the charts, and all four coins are now testing the upper edges of the ranges they built since August.

Why Crypto Is Rising After the Fed and CLARITY Shock

In early June, the same four coins sank together while stocks hit records. This time they are rising together, and the reasons are mostly regulatory and macro.

Pantera Capital founder Dan Morehead told The Block that the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) are already putting in place much of what the failed bill promised.

"The industry doesn't need Congress," he said.

Macro pressure also eased. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed back above 5% after the Fed decision, then gave some of that move back as oil pulled away from its highs, according to Nexo's daily market dispatch.

The Bank of Japan's 25 basis point hike, the last major central bank event of the week, passed without a new selloff.

Derivatives traders lean the same way. Andrew Melville, head of research at Block Scholes, said in a note that short-dated implied volatility for Bitcoin and Ether fell strongly once the week's event risks passed.

He added that 7-day volatility smiles are "skewed strongly towards bullish positioning in call options."

Bitcoin Price Prediction: $82,600 Is the Last Barrier Before $100,000

Bitcoin is doing what I described in my golden cross analysis this morning. It bounced from the bottom of its range near $75,300 and is now attacking the top.

The 50-day EMA at $73,986 stays above the 200-day line at $73,234, so the golden cross that formed on September 12 is intact.

The level that decides the next leg is $82,614, the upper edge of a resistance band that reaches about $84,400. Price has stalled below it several times since late August, as I noted in my September 7 Bitcoin forecast.

A daily close above the band would open my target zone at $98,068 to $99,486, about 21% to 23% above today's price.

If the breakout fails again, the range floor at $75,339 is the first support, 6.9% below the current price. A daily close under it would put $66,780 back in play.

Ethereum Tests the Top of Its Range at $2,616

Ether has spent most of the time since the late August breakout between $2,393 and $2,616, a range just over 9% wide. Today's high of $2,609 took it to the very top of that box. The 50-day EMA at $2,295 already runs above the 200-day EMA at $2,213, which supports the upside case.

The rally started from the base I described in my July Ethereum analysis, when ETH cleared its year-long downtrend.

title: S&P Global to Acquire OpenZeppelin in Crypto Infrastructure Expanding Effort
summary:
Key Takeaways: S&P Global has agreed to acquire OpenZeppelin to boost its crypto and onchain risk capabilities. Over $37 trillion of value is being transacted via OpenZeppelin’s Contracts library. The
The post S&P Global to Acquire OpenZeppelin in Crypto Infrastructure Expanding Effort appeared firs...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • S&P Global has agreed to acquire OpenZeppelin to boost its crypto and onchain risk capabilities.
  • Over $37 trillion of value is being transacted via OpenZeppelin’s Contracts library.
  • The company has resolved 900+ security lapses and found 10,000+ vulnerabilities prior production.

S&P Global is expanding further into crypto infrastructure through an agreement to acquire blockchain security firm OpenZeppelin. The transaction brings smart contract security into S&P Global’s growing digital asset business as financial products and market infrastructure increasingly move onchain.

  • S&P Global Adds Smart Contract Security to Crypto Strategy
  • Security Moves Closer to the Center of Onchain Finance
    • OpenZeppelin Will Continue Under Its Own Name

S&P Global Adds Smart Contract Security to Crypto Strategy

Founded in 2015, OpenZeppelin has become a major security provider for blockchain developers, DeFi protocols and financial institutions. It leverages open source smart contract libraries, expert security evaluations, and developer services.

The OpenZeppelin Contracts library has been used by infrastructure that has facilitated over $37 trillion in value transferred, the companies said. The library is utilized in a variety of blockchain apps, including behind many major stablecoins and tokenized funds.

Aside from that OpenZeppelin has been able to manage over 900 security engagements for protocols and institutions involving digital assets. These encounters have uncovered over 10,000 vulnerabilities preproduction, showcasing its magnitude in catching risks before blockchain applications enter production.

Read More: $5.87M Ethereum Exploit Hits TrustedVolumes as 1inch Denies Any Protocol Breach

Security Moves Closer to the Center of Onchain Finance

The purchase puts S&P Global under a technology-risk layer directly under the financial products with crypto or tokenization.

OpenZeppelin’s deeper skill and expertise will augment S&P’s existing reference points on risk assessment of smart contracts and onchain technology, S&P Global said. The combined capabilities can address risks to the blockchain infrastructure and the code of that asset in addition to the financial traits of the asset.

This happens especially with stablecoins, tokenized funds, and DeFi applications, where asset transfers, ownership, and other essential capabilities are managed by smart contracts.

While markets move onto blockchain infrastructure, S&P Global Ratings’ digital asset strategy is centered on trusted data, benchmarks and transparent risk assessment, said Yann Le Pallec, the firm’s president.

The partnership makes sense for crypto markets: combining OpenZeppelin’s onchain risk assessment and security background with S&P Global’s extensive experience with financial-market risk assessment.

OpenZeppelin Will Continue Under Its Own Name

OpenZeppelin will operate as a standalone business under the umbrella of S&P Global, and be known as OpenZeppelin. Brener is awaiting instructions from Le Pallec as his CEO.

The parties have not been specifying price figures of the deal. Closing is subject to customary conditions, and S&P Global indicated that the deal will not materially affect the companies’ finances.

The transaction also does not affect OpenZeppelin’s key position in the crypto space. Its security skills are already in use by blockchain networks, DeFi protocols, institutions and enterprises.

OpenZeppelin’s standards and technology already allows for infrastructure behind the stablecoins, tokenized funds, DeFi protocols, and other on-chain markets, Brener said. It would further this foundation to more organisations entering digital assets, he added, while speaking with S&P Global.

The acquisition also gives OpenZeppelin access to S&P Global’s institutional relationships and global distribution, potentially bringing its security services and technology to a broader financial-market audience.

title: Zcash Sets NU7 for November With 25-Second Blocks and Major Network Changes
summary:
Key Takeaways: The teams behind Zcash have decided to aim for the November 5, 2026 target date for NU7 activation on the mainnet. NU7 will reduce the target block from
The post Zcash Sets NU7 for November With 25-Second Blocks and Major Network Changes appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The teams behind Zcash have decided to aim for the November 5, 2026 target date for NU7 activation on the mainnet.
  • NU7 will reduce the target block from 75 seconds to 25 seconds.
  • The upgrade will ensure that the issuance of ZEC halvings continue and incorporate the Network Sustainability Mechanism.

The developers and engineering teams come to a consensus regarding the next significant upgrade to Zcash in the NU7 package and schedule for network upgrades. The upgrade is expected to introduce quicker block production, modifications to transaction compatibility and emerging strategies that look into network sustainability.

  • NU7 Sets a 25-Second Block Target
  • Faster Blocks Bring Infrastructure Changes
    • Zcash Keeps the Halving Schedule
    • NU7 Timeline Moves Into Testing

NU7 Sets a 25-Second Block Target

According to Zcash developer Sean Bowe and the Zcash Community Forum, NU7 is scheduled to reach the official testnet on October 6, followed by a targeted mainnet activation on November 5. A final decision on the mainnet activation height is scheduled for October 20, after the ecosystem has reviewed how NU7 performs on testnet.

NU7 is coming! All of the Zcash development orgs have come to unanimous agreement about the contents and timeline of our next network upgrade, following the sentiment collection results earlier this week.

Activation approximately November 5.

Learn more:https://t.co/3pSKptV9gO

— Sean Bowe (@ebfull) September 17, 2026

The most impactful technical change is the change in block spacing from 75 seconds to 25 seconds with the passing of ZIP-218.

That threefold reduction is proposed to reduce the transaction confirmation latency. The ZIP suggests the reduced interval will lead to a better experience for transactions that require one or two confirmations, as well as to an increase in the bandwidth of consensus.

Read More: Arc Mainnet Goes Live With 190+ Partners, BlackRock and Visa Back New Network

Faster Blocks Bring Infrastructure Changes

This isn’t just going to be a matter of the timers, the faster block schedule will be applied to the encryption of blocks. Zcash developers also have proposed the necessary changes in the network parameters to ensure similar time-based behavior post-NU7.

For example, the proposal ZIP-218 suggests increasing the proof-of-work goldrush window from 17 to 102 blocks. The number of blocks increases but the smoothing time remains close to the wall clock time wanted.

This upgrade might need a bit of help from the full nodes, indexers and block explorers too. Ordinary wallets would not see major modifications as NU7 does not work with new types of transactions, developers said.

Zcash Keeps the Halving Schedule

Furthermore, based on the newest community sentiment results, there will be some changes on Network Sustainability Mechanism for Zcash on NU7.

In this direction, the existing ZEC halving structure is maintained, and the previously stopped issuance will return in February 2031. The network upgrade will also be removing transaction version 4.

The decision was based on talks with several organizations and engineering teams within the Zcash ecosystem, such as the Zcash Foundation, Tachyon, Valar, ZODL, and Shielded Labs.

The community sentiment collection took place earlier this September. The reported results demonstrated that the 25 seconds blocks and keeping the halving schedule were supported.

NU7 Timeline Moves Into Testing

The features are planned to be implemented and available on the testnet by September 30, which is the deadline for this release.

The next one is on October 6, with the official Zcash testnet that will activate NU7. The developers will then gain experience on the testnet and then decide on the final mainnet activation on October 20.

With the current timeline, NU7 will activate on the Zcash mainnet on November 5, 2026.

title: Ripple Says $XRP, RLUSD Could Turn 24/7 Crypto Into a CFO Treasury Tool
summary:
Key Takeaways: CFOs are no longer questioning digital assets as speculative but by practical use, according to Ripple. XRP and RLUSD are set to be used in treasury, payroll and
The post Ripple Says $XRP, RLUSD Could Turn 24/7 Crypto Into a CFO Treasury Tool appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • CFOs are no longer questioning digital assets as speculative but by practical use, according to Ripple.
  • XRP and RLUSD are set to be used in treasury, payroll and cross border payment flows.
  • 24/7 onchain liquidity markets may enable companies to become more flexible in controlling their liquidity.

Ripple is highlighting a change in how corporate finance teams view crypto, with digital assets increasingly being discussed as operational tools rather than assets held purely for speculation. In a recent post on X, the company pointed to XRP and RLUSD as examples of assets that could support treasury operations, payroll and cross-border flows.

CFOs have moved from viewing digital assets as purely speculative to having utility.

The opportunity now is what crypto and stablecoins, like $XRP and $RLUSD, can do for treasury, payroll, and cross-border flows.

The game-changer: onchain markets don’t stop at 5 pm or take… pic.twitter.com/3lnAQT1lQV

— Ripple (@Ripple) September 17, 2026

  • Crypto Moves Into Corporate Treasury
  • 24/7 Markets Change the Treasury Clock
    • XRP and RLUSD Target Different Payment Needs

Crypto Moves Into Corporate Treasury

The CFO conversation has shifted and the question is not just what digital assets are worth, but what they can do for a business, per Ripple.

According to the company, CFOs have shifted their perception of digital assets from a “purely speculative” asset to a useful asset. The change brings treasury into the conversation, as companies place, control and optimize cash and liquidity, payments and short-turn funding.

XRP and RLUSD are two different types of digital assets in Ripple’s ecosystem. XRP is the native cryptocurrency of the XRP Ledger and can be used as a bridge asset for transactions. The U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin, on the other hand, is Ripple’s Ripple Dollar stablecoin (RLUSD).

For corporate finance teams, that distinction is important. Different treasury needs can be satisfied by a volatile crypto asset and a stable coin that uses dollars as the underlying asset.

Read More: Ripple Puts XRP on Louisville Courts, Expanding Its $5M College Sports Push

24/7 Markets Change the Treasury Clock

Ripple is also involved in one key difference amid onchain markets and financial infrastructure, with 24/7 operations.

Business hours/weekends and settlement windows may limit traditional banking processes. These can occur outside those schedules, too, providing yet another avenue for the movement of liquidity when traditional modes aren’t available to treasury teams.

This is the concept behind Ripple’s own treasury system. It has a unified platform where digital assets and fiat liquidity exist on the same ledger, and teams can monitor and manage both types on a single platform.

But companies don’t necessarily have to swap-in traditional cash handling for blockchain cash management. Rather, digital assets can serve as a new instrument of liquidity in addition to existing treasury systems.

XRP and RLUSD Target Different Payment Needs

One thing that Ripple is suitable to point out is cross-border transactions. The company claims that the use of blockchain technology can cut delays stemming from correspondent banking and get value across borders within seconds.

Currently, Ripple Payments is supporting treasury and liquidity management, payroll, payments to suppliers and other cross-border use cases. It can operate on both XRP and stablecoins (RLUSD) depending on the transaction or need for liquidity.

RLUSD is especially suited to transactions where the maintaining of a dollar-denominated value is important. The stablecoin is backed by cash, U.S. Treasuries and cash equivalents, claims Ripple, adding that redemption is available at par.

If it’s payroll, it implies relocating funds across borders without relying on traditional banking windows, and the recipient can now get stablecoins portions or transform their into regional currency through sustained compensation structure.

Ripple has also been building treasury products around this use case. In April, the company launched Digital Asset Accounts and Unified Treasury, allowing CFOs and treasury teams to view, hold, receive and manage fiat and digital liquidity within one platform.

The latest comments therefore fit into a broader push by Ripple to bring XRP, stablecoins and blockchain settlement deeper into everyday corporate finance, moving crypto use beyond trading and investment into payments, liquidity and treasury management.

title: SEC Clears Path for Tokenized Stocks With 5-Year Onchain Trading Exemption
summary:
Key Takeaways: The SEC has introduced a five-year “Innovation Exemption” to permit trading of U.S. stocks by tokenizing them on approved venues. With a permissioned AMM liquidity pool, Tokenized Securities
The post SEC Clears Path for Tokenized Stocks With 5-Year Onchain Trading Exemption appeared f...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The SEC has introduced a five-year “Innovation Exemption” to permit trading of U.S. stocks by tokenizing them on approved venues.
  • With a permissioned AMM liquidity pool, Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) can comply with investor protection’s necessary rules.
  • With onchain securities trading, the agency is looking to receive public input on considered permanent rules.

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has unveiled a new regulatory framework that could accelerate the adoption of tokenized stocks in the United States.

On September 17, the agency announced a temporary “Innovation Exemption” that grants conditional relief to Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs), allowing them to facilitate trading of tokenized National Market System (NMS) stocks through blockchain-based infrastructure.

  • SEC Opens Door to Onchain Stock Trading
  • Key Rules for Tokenized Securities Venues
    • Compliance Requirements
    • Liquidity Providers Also Receive Relief

SEC Opens Door to Onchain Stock Trading

Property tax exemption is granted for the operation of TSV as a “not a traditional exchange” under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

Permissioned automated market makers (AMMs) and liquidity pools can facilitate the assembly of sellers and buyers for tokenized stocks in these venues. The framework is aimed at providing protections for investors and the marketplace, while encouraging innovation,” the SEC said.

SEC Commissioner Paul Atkins called it a vital step forward in modernizing U.S. capital markets and allowing regulated onchain trading for some equity securities. The exemption is temporary and runs for five years from the date of publication, unless the exemptions are to be revoked by further regulation.

Read More: SEC Eyes Tokenized Stocks Plan That Could Unlock Trillions in Crypto Trading Markets

Key Rules for Tokenized Securities Venues

The SEC placed several conditions on the relief. TSVs must ensure that tokenized shares have the same rights and privileges as the underlying shares. Capitals on number of symbols listed, and trading volume, also for platforms.

Compliance Requirements

TVS must meet several critical requirements under the order. To support tokenized stock trading, smart contracts should be open, verifiable and built on a public permissionless chain.

If the underlying stock is suspended from the main exchange, trading of tokenized shares should be suspended. Platforms must also make public information on their trading activities and operations. Further, before an unaffiliated third party tokenizes a company’s shares, the issuer would have to be alerted and provided an opportunity to object.

While the SEC noted that the measures are geared toward safeguarding investors, they also enable experimentation with possible blockchain-based structures of markets.

Liquidity Providers Also Receive Relief

Additionally, the order provides conditional exemption from issuance of “dealer” registration for liquidity providers in TSV-registered liquidity pools.

This applies to the participants who offer liquidity through their own capital and could add to what is described as typical market-making activity. Expect the exemption to have a positive impact on liquidity for token-based stock trading venues during the pilot.

The SEC is seeking public comment on any aspects of the framework, such as proposed amendments and further action.

The announcement is one of an unmistakable move by regulators in the U.S. to expand blockchain-based security markets. The framework is a temporary solution, but it does offer a clear process for trading tokenized securities as traditional financial assets advance onto blockchain networks.
